lines.trans: How did you find me, Ainura?
I have been working for you for a long time.
I know all your secret places.
All right, and why did you come?
Dear Chef, you need to return to the kitchen.
You sound right now like my former mother-in-law.
Seriously, it is very hard for the cooks without you.
They are not coping at all with orders.
The new female chef will soon fall completely ill.
Are you sure you are not deceiving me?
When have I ever lied to you?
All right, let us drink to victory then.
Chef, I am at work after all!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'victory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Люди в городе аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People in the town are applauding your victory!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
Secondary conversational sense ('post, position') (на его место = in his place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: with present: Я давно здесь = I've been here a long time
Secondary conversational sense ('long ago') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to lie to') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Потому что она простая. Её все обманывают.
examples.trans: Because she's naive. Everybody cheats her.

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up
Secondary conversational sense ('come on') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('bye, see you') (casual goodbye) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ dative: мне тяжело = it's hard for me
Secondary conversational sense ('heavily') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: It's hard for you right now.

examples.text: Аркаша, я понимаю, тебе сейчас тяжело. Но…
examples.trans: Arkasha, I understand, it's hard for you right now. But...

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
imperfective, governs с + instrumental

examples.text: Он легко справлялся с любой задачей.
examples.trans: He easily coped with any task.
Do not argue, Fedya managed somehow!

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.trans: In short, girls, listen to me.
Girl, pass me the sugar, please.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.
Secondary conversational sense ('in general') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'when'.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда ты наконец принесёшь горячий соус на раздачу?
examples.trans: When will you finally bring the hot sauce to the pass?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mother-in-law (wife's mother)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если бы вы моей тёщей были, я бы терпел.
examples.trans: If you were my mother-in-law, I would put up with you.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, если бы вы моей тёщей были! Тогда я бы терпел.
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, if you were my mother-in-law! Then I would put up with you.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, если бы вы моей тёщей были!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, if you were my mother-in-law!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

заболеть.gloss: to fall ill, to get sick

meanings.en: to fall ill, to come down with an illness
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall ill, to get sick', paired with 'болеть'.

examples.text: Вчера он заболел и остался дома.
examples.trans: Yesterday he fell ill and stayed at home.

examples.text: А у меня учительница по математике заболела.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not at all') (совсем не) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'seriously'.
бывший мэр = the former mayor; бывшая жена = ex-wife

examples.text: Мне нужно немножко поработать с бывшим мэром.
examples.trans: I need to do a little work on the former mayor.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: In the kitchen they are preparing this order.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('secret, hidden').

examples.text: Тогда я сама выберу другое тайное место.
examples.trans: Then I will choose another secret place myself.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

выпить.gloss: to drink, to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: often used without an object for drinking alcohol

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
